title: South Korea's Lee says hopes reopening talks with North Korea could lead to lasting peace
html:
FILE PHOTO: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung speaks at the 2026 APEC CEO Summit held ahead of the APEC China 2026 summit in Shenzhen, southern China’s Guangdong province on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Ng Han Guan/Pool via REUTERS/File Photo

SEOUL, Nov 19 - South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Thursday he hoped a reopening of dialogue with North Korea would lead to discussions on ending the Korean War and establishing a lasting peace, as he addressed Asia-Pacific leaders in China.

Speaking at a session of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, Lee said peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula were essential to shared regional prosperity and urged members to take an active interest and cooperate, according to the Korean presidential office.

His statement came ahead of a trilateral summit between the leaders of Russia, China and the United States at APEC, with some analysts saying North Korea's nuclear weapons and sanctions on Pyongyang could be among the issues discussed.

South Korea's National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac told a briefing on Wednesday that Chinese President Xi Jinping told Lee at talks on the sidelines of the summit that Beijing would play a constructive role to realise peace on the Korean Peninsula.

Lee also held a meeting with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday at the summit, where they agreed to cooperate on building stable and mutually beneficial energy supply chains, according to Lee's office. REUTERS
summary: SEOUL, Nov 19 - South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Thursday he hoped a reopening of dialogue with North Korea would lead to discussions on ending the Korean War and establishing a lasting peace, as he addressed Asia-Pacific leaders in China.
